I’ve seen many riots and spoken to rioters and their victims. A pattern emerges. Young people, some flushed with fury about injustice, others exuberant with the thrill of violence, smash windows, burn buildings and loot shops. In the aftermath life gets worse. Investors and insurers shun the worst-affected areas, so jobs vanish and groceries become costlier. I’ve seen this story play out from Lesotho to Louisiana. So I doubt that the rioters in France will build a fairer society. Torching public schools is an odd way to try. As we argue in our cover package this week, protesters across Europe have plenty of genuine complaints. Recent riots have not, as MAGA pundits breathlessly speculate, been led by Islamists or masses of rowdy immigrants. They are largely home-grown, and focus on bread-and-butter issues. People are fed up with high prices and meagre job opportunities. They want more subsidies, better public services and someone else to pay for it all. And therein lies the snag. Growth has been feeble and public finances are a mess, especially in France, despite its clout in Brussels. When Emmanuel Macron, its centrist president, faced huge gilets jaunes demonstrations in 2018-19, he was able to placate protesters with handouts. This time, with public debt perilously high, he cannot meet their demands. So they will stay angry. Worse, they seem likely to embrace the politicians of the populist left and right, who promise goodies for all from the magic money tree, plus early retirement if you don’t like working. Next year France may elect as president Marine Le Pen, who pledges both implausible spending and public order, with a hint that disorder is largely caused by, you know, people whose ancestors weren’t Gauls. The political centre in Europe is in serious trouble. Voters are frustrated, and tempted to try something radically different. Germany’s pedestrian chancellor has no answer for the nationalist-right Alice Weidel, who wants to cut off support for Ukraine. Spain’s centre-left prime minister will probably be turfed out soon. Italy’s far right is on the march. Europe’s more extreme parties have no serious plans to revive growth and—obviously—no access to a magic money tree. 81294.subject: The One-Person Company on Grok Bot 🤖
81294.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/one-person-company-grok-bot

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
In September, three people from SpaceXSI sat down in a San Francisco studio with an empty GitHub org, an empty Slack, and no idea. Their plan was to build a company live with Grok Bot. Seventy-two hours later, they had shipped a game, Thursday Arena, from a brand-new X account with a blank profile picture. On stream, they reported more than 400 merged pull requests, about 2,000 players on launch day, and the top Google result for the game’s name. Not too shabby! 👏
Yet, revenue was $0. A bot that had been told to spend the whole day making money also made nothing 🤷‍♂️
That number is probably the most useful thing to come out of the entire Grok Bot Galaxy event. The team proved that a few people with bots can build, test, ship, support, and market a product in days. They also proved that bots don’t decide what to build, don’t make anyone care, and don’t close a sale. In the closing retrospective, Roshan Sadanani named “getting people to care” as the hardest part of building anything, even with unlimited AI.
More importantly, it also sets the brief for a one-person company in late 2026. A one-person company runs on Grok Bot when every recurring function (customers, product, support, launch) has a bot that owns it, a source of truth it works from, and a line it can’t cross without the founder. The founder keeps the three jobs bots can’t do: deciding what to build, selling it, and saying no.
The timing matters because in the past 6 weeks, Grok Bot has added Team Bots, a proactive Primary Bot, read-only bank data, purchases with approval, an email address of its own and, since October, a move to Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/d6e6fbab-b52d-4acf-b2f8-95c90861e794?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] underneath. Each removes another reason to hire your first employees, and each widens what a careless setup can break.
Our Ultimate Guide to Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/39e77e2f-c856-4d77-9839-90bb56686364?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] explained how the product works and how to set up a first Bot. How to Hire a Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/fbb09996-9b23-4b8a-a6f9-cfdaa9c98d7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] showed how to manage one like an employee, with role cards, probation, and promotion.
This piece goes a level up: how to run a whole company on them, function by function, built from what SpaceXSI’s team did on stream, including what broke. Inside:
5 lessons from the 72-hour build that matter for solo founders, including the one the hosts only admitted at the end.

Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** AI agents are logging into bank accounts, and some banks can't tell whether you sent them. October keeps stacking up hacks, so people started calling it Black October. Outside auditors found holes in how OpenAI watches its own agents, but OpenAI got to cut whatever it considered sensitive from their public report. And Claude is about to stop asking your permission for every step.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Banks:** Can your bank tell if your AI agent went rogue?

* **Black October:** Did this month's hacks hit an app you use?

* **OpenAI:** What did OpenAI black out of an outside audit?

* **Claude:** What will Claude do without asking you first?


----------







----------
## Banks can't tell your AI agent from a rogue one

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/649fa79d-21d0-4c55-adbe-1f19d8ef693f/97dfe5b1-9d85-457f-8d78-ef4ac2ea4e61.jpg?t=1792743716)
Caption: 

One bank executive [told Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/22/ai-agents-banks-unauthorized-accounts-access) they struggle to work out whether an AI agent inside a customer's account was sent by that customer or went rogue.

Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo are racing to contain agents showing up in accounts. Some already know of unauthorized agents getting in.

Most of these agents log in with the customer's own username and password. Even with your OK, that breaks the rules at most banks, which want a human to log in.

* Some agents called bank call centers or seemed to act without being told to.

* Executives called it horrifying, and Morgan Stanley has started blocking outside agents.

* Most banks are moving to read-only access, so agents can see your money but can't move it.

* JPMorgan's finance chief warned you could face the consequences if an agent you gave your login to made a transaction you didn't want.

Chase's advice is to never give your username and password to anyone, AI included.

Bernie Sanders called it insane and wants AI paused now.

Banks are already planning for the day after the worst happens, so they can quickly lock down accounts or give customers their access back.

Two days ago, on October 20, 2026, a comment window closed in Washington that almost nobody in real estate was watching. The SEC had proposed Regulation Crypto Assets back in August, a tailored offering framework for crypto assets. Crypto media called it the green light. Threads went up. "The SEC finally opened the door." Then came the part nobody quoted. The proposal reaches only investment contracts involving a non-security crypto asset and nothing else. A token tied to a building, a commodity, or a royalty stream falls entirely outside it. Your property token was never in scope. If you are sitting on real assets and waiting for Washington to make tokenization simple, that wait just got longer. Meanwhile, one Gulf government has been running a live tokenized property market for over a year. What the SEC Actually Said, and What It Did Not Three separate things happened in 2026, and the market keeps collapsing them into one. They are not the same. Read the last column down the table. Not one of those three created a new route for a tokenized building. The SEC's position has been consistent and it is worth stating plainly: moving an activity on-chain does not move it outside the securities laws. So How Do You Actually Tokenize Property In The US? The same way you did before any of this. Through exemptions that have existed for decades. Regulation D 506(c). Permits broad advertising, restricts buyers to accredited investors Regulation S. Capital raises outside the US with no SEC registration, as long as US persons are excluded Regulation A+. Opens the door to non-accredited investors, with lower raise ceilings and more disclosure Transfer agent oversight, accredited checks, resale restrictions. Not optional extras. The structure itself Most serious platforms run Reg D and Reg S together, reaching domestic accredited investors and global buyers at the same time. There is no shortcut arriving. There is only whether your token model was designed to fit these rules or bolted onto them afterward. The Market Did Not Wait For Clarity While the frameworks argue with each other, the money moved.
